abstract: The immune system can recognize and eliminate tumor cells through the secretion of specific cytokines, including TRAIL (tumor necrosis factor-related apoptosis-inducing ligand). TRAIL triggers apoptosis by binding to its death receptors, TRAIL-R1 and TRAIL-R2. However, cancer cells can evade TRAIL-mediated cell death through the expression of decoy receptors, TRAIL-R3 and TRAIL-R4, which can bind TRAIL but lack the ability to initiate apoptotic signaling. Here, we focused on the decoy receptor TRAIL-R4, also known as TNFRSF10D, and investigated an alternative splicing event that generates a transcript lacking exon 3. This exon-skipping event results in a truncated receptor isoform, termed iTRAIL-R4, which lacks part of the ligand-binding domain. Structural biology analyses confirmed that TRAIL cannot efficiently bind to iTRAIL-R4. Interestingly, whereas the canonical TRAIL-R4 isoform protects cancer cells against TRAIL-induced apoptosis, overexpression of iTRAIL-R4 sensitizes cancer cells to TRAIL-mediated cell death. Furthermore, combining iTRAIL-R4 expression with different therapeutic treatments enhances the sensitivity of cancer cells. Collectively, our findings highlight the potential of iTRAIL-R4 to help counteract therapeutic cancer resistance and recurrence. They further support the therapeutic relevance of modulating TRAIL-R4 alternative splicing to shift cancer cells toward a more apoptosis-sensitive state.

summary: A TRAIL-R4 exon-3-skipping isoform (iTRAIL-R4) fails to bind TRAIL and sensitizes cancer cells to TRAIL-induced apoptosis, unlike canonical TRAIL-R4.
